title: When ‘Urgent’ Doesn’t Mean ‘Important’
scene: Several tasks arrive at the same time, and they all seem urgent. Instead of reacting to the loudest request, you compare what would actually happen if each task had to wait and choose based on impact.
sceneJa: いくつもの仕事が同時に飛んできて、全部が急ぎに見える。いちばん強く急かされているものに反応するのではなく、後回しにした場合の影響を比べて優先順位を決める。

chunks.en: When several requests came in at once,
chunks.ja: いくつもの依頼が一度に入ってきたとき
最初に直感的に思ったのは
どれであれ、それに対応することでした
一番急ぎに見えるものに
実際に何が起きるのか

chunks.en: if each task had to wait,
chunks.ja: それぞれの仕事を待たせた場合
一番強く急かされている依頼が

chunks.en: wasn’t necessarily the most important one.
chunks.ja: 必ずしも一番重要ではないと
ある仕事は問題なく待たせられます

chunks.en: while another would delay three other people
chunks.ja: 一方、別の仕事は3人を遅らせることになります
私がそれを終わらせないままにしたら
そこで、〜と考える代わりに
何に一番早く返事すべきか
私は考えるようになりました

chunks.en: what would have the biggest impact
chunks.ja: 何が一番大きな影響を持つのか
もし何もしなかったら

questions.question: Which boundary is most natural?
options: I realized / that the loudest request / wasn’t necessarily the most important one
I realized that / the loudest / request wasn’t necessarily / the most important one
I / realized that the loudest request wasn’t / necessarily the most important one
questions.explanation: ‘I realized’ sets up the discovery, and the that-clause gives the content of what the speaker realized.

questions.question: What does ‘while’ mean in this passage?
options: On the other hand / in contrast
questions.explanation: Here ‘while’ contrasts two tasks: one can wait, whereas the other would delay three people.

questions.question: How does the speaker finally decide what to prioritize?
options: Choose the task from the person asking most loudly
Choose whichever task looks fastest to finish
Consider which task would have the biggest impact if left undone
questions.explanation: The speaker shifts from visible urgency to consequences, asking what would happen if nothing were done.

speak: Start slightly rushed, as if several requests have just arrived at once. Slow down at ‘But after checking what would actually happen’ and become more deliberate. Finish ‘what would have the biggest impact if I did nothing’ calmly, as if the speaker has moved from reacting to choosing.
review: Previous flow: deadline → condition → trade-off → alternative → decision. Today’s flow: reaction → consequence → comparison → priority. The key shift is from asking ‘What looks most urgent?’ to asking ‘What happens if I do nothing?’
